digest.component_or_area: bug lifecycle / transition close / dependency linking
propositions: On bug close, auto-derive a caused_by link to a culprit ticket by git-blaming the pre-fix state (fixing-commit~1) over file_impact, resolving the dominant commit's rebar-ticket trailer only when >50% of blamed lines point to a single commit.
The auto-derivation skips (returns None) when file_impact is absent, no fixing commit is found, the blame is ambiguous (no >50% dominant commit), or the dominant commit has no rebar-ticket trailer.

An explicit --caused-by <id> parameter at close time overrides auto-derivation; the link is written via _write_link_event directly, bypassing the closed-source guard that would normally reject links from closed sources.

The caused_by link is written after the bug is closed (after txn.transition_core commits STATUS), so the direct-writer path is required to defeat the source_status == "closed" rejection in graph._links.add_dependency.
The public library transition() facade in _lib_writes.py must thread a caused_by parameter end-to-end (via transition_compute) so non-CLI callers can set caused_by on close.
The bug-template includes a blame-hunt advisory explaining when auto-derivation applies and when to use --caused-by explicitly.
